roles.heroLead: Builder-grade showers were tiled to pass a walkthrough, not twenty winters on the Ridge. Tile and grout only shed water — the bonded membrane behind them is what stops it. We build that hidden assembly properly, flood-test it a full 24 hours, photograph the proof, and only then set tile.
roles.costH2: How much does tile installation cost in Snoqualmie, WA?
roles.costP1: Figure $14–$26 per square foot installed for Snoqualmie tile work, covering labor, tile, substrate prep and setting materials — labor on its own starts at $11/sq ft. Tub-shower surrounds generally run $3,200–$6,800; a full bathroom with shower, floor and niche lands in the $6,500–$14,000 range, and a stand-alone bathroom floor (about 45 sq ft) sits between $900 and $1,600.
roles.costP2: What moves the bid isn't the tile's price tag — it's the format. Trendy mosaic sheets at $4 can out-cost a $12 large-format plank once installed, since every extra cut and grout line is labor, and labor is most of what you're paying for.
roles.costNote: Snoqualmie-area installed ranges, current August 2026, covering tile, materials and labor. Your written on-site quote is the number to trust.
roles.layersLead: Count them: seven layers under and behind your tile. The failed showers we open are missing one — the membrane, nearly every time — because somebody saved a few hundred dollars on build day and left the next owner a five-figure teardown.
roles.whyP1: A shortcut shower fails on a schedule: water slips past grout, sits in the substrate, and announces itself years later — a soft hallway floor, a stain blooming on the ceiling below — often just after the builder's warranty runs out. By then you're rebuilding framing, subfloor and drywall before any new tile.
roles.whyP2: Waterproofing runs about a tenth of what a shower costs. Cutting it is how a builder saves hundreds and an owner later spends tens of thousands.
roles.scopeIntro: Prices below are starting points — format, substrate and layout complexity all move them. The binding number gets written at your place, free.
roles.cardShower: The full assembly in order: pre-sloped base, bonded membrane, a photographed flood test, then niche, curb or curbless entry and tile. The invisible half is the half that matters.
roles.cardFloors: Bathrooms, kitchens, mudrooms, entries and basements — subfloor brought flat first, with an uncoupling membrane wherever radiant heat or movement asks for it.
roles.cardBacksplash: Slab-look porcelain, herringbone, subway or mosaic sheet. Outlets cut clean, edges trimmed, grout keyed to the countertop instead of whatever came in the box.
roles.cardHeated: Radiant mat on an uncoupling membrane, resistance-checked before setting and again after, running on a dedicated circuit. Worth doing only while the floor's already open.
roles.cardRepair: Cracked field tile, failing grout, shower corners letting go. You'll get a straight answer on whether it's fixable or the substrate underneath is done.
roles.cardDemo: Old surround, thinset and backer board out — dust boxed in behind plastic and negative air, debris hauled the same day. The driveway stays yours.

roles.faqQ1: How much does tile installation cost in Snoqualmie, WA?
roles.faqA1: Tile work in Snoqualmie prices out at $14–$26 per square foot installed once you total labor, tile, setting materials and substrate prep; labor alone opens at $11 per square foot. Typical numbers: $3,200–$6,800 for a tub-shower surround, $900–$1,600 for a bathroom floor of around 45 sq ft, and $6,500–$14,000 for a complete bathroom covering floor, shower and niche. The format you pick swings cost harder than the tile price does — mosaics and large-format both eat labor that a 12×12 doesn't.
roles.faqQ2: How much does a tiled shower cost in Snoqualmie?
roles.faqA2: A standard alcove shower in Snoqualmie budgets out at $3,200–$6,800. That covers tearing out the old surround, a pre-sloped pan with the waterproofing system bonded over it, the tile work, a niche and grout. Steam showers, benches, curbless entries and full-height stone push higher. The waterproofing piece is roughly ten percent of the bill — and it's the ten percent standing between you and a five-figure framing repair.
roles.faqQ3: Do you waterproof showers before tiling?
roles.faqA3: Every time — that step is most of the reason we get hired. You get a pre-sloped base, an ANSI A118.10 bonded membrane carried up the walls to TCNA methods, corners, seams and pipe penetrations sealed, and a 24-hour flood test documented in photos before a single tile goes up. Neither tile nor grout is waterproof; the membrane behind them is what protects the framing.
roles.faqQ4: How long does a bathroom tile job take?
roles.faqA4: Four to six working days is standard for a Snoqualmie bathroom: demo and dust walls on day one, substrate plus waterproofing on day two with the flood test running 24 hours behind it, tile setting for a day or two, then grout, silicone and trim to finish. Keep the shower dry another 24 hours while grout cures. A floor on its own usually takes one or two days.
roles.faqQ5: Porcelain or ceramic tile — which is better?
roles.faqA5: For floors, showers and anywhere wet or hard-worked, porcelain — denser, tougher against chips, and under 0.5% water absorption. Ceramic is the economical pick for walls and backsplashes and does fine there. Our default spec in Snoqualmie: porcelain on every floor and shower floor, ceramic or glass where the only job is looking good on a wall.
roles.faqQ6: Can you install a heated tile floor?
roles.faqA6: Yes. On a foggy Ridge morning a warm tile floor stops feeling like a luxury fast. Electric radiant adds $11–$16 per square foot installed, thermostat included, laid on an uncoupling membrane with resistance tests before and after tiling, and wired to its own circuit. The only economical moment to add it is while the floor is already torn up — so decide before the remodel, not after.
roles.faqQ7: Do I need to remove the old tile first?
roles.faqA7: Almost always. Removal and haul-away start at $3.50 per square foot, and demo is the one chance to inspect the subfloor for movement or hidden water damage — the exact things a twenty-year-old builder install likes to conceal — and to keep the new floor height correct at doorways. Tiling over tile is technically possible on a flat, sound, well-bonded surface, but it hides problems we'd much rather find early.
roles.faqQ8: How much does a kitchen backsplash cost in Snoqualmie?
roles.faqA8: In Snoqualmie a standard 30 sq ft kitchen backsplash runs $1,100–$2,200 installed, with outlet holes cut, edges trimmed and grout tuned to the counter. Layout drives where you land in that range: herringbone, mosaic sheets, picture-frame details behind the range and full-height slab-look porcelain all add cutting and layout time.
roles.faqQ9: Can you fix cracked tile or regrout instead of replacing?
roles.faqA9: Frequently. Repairs and regrouting start at $8 per square foot — the move when grout has stained or started crumbling, when an impact cracked a tile or two, or when shower corners need old grout swapped for silicone. The wrong call is patching over a failed substrate: hollow-sounding tile, pieces loosening in a pattern, a wall with any give. That buys months, not years — and we'll tell you which situation you have before quoting.
roles.faqQ10: Which Snoqualmie neighborhoods do you tile?
roles.faqA10: Everywhere in town — Snoqualmie Ridge, downtown Snoqualmie, Kimball Creek and Meadowbrook — plus the Valley around it: Fall City, North Bend, Preston, Carnation, Si View, Tanner, Riverbend, Wilderness Rim, Lake Alice and up to Snoqualmie Pass. Mirrormont, the Issaquah Highlands and the rest of the Eastside are an easy run too.
roles.faqQ11: What warranty comes with tile installation?
roles.faqA11: OC Flooring's tile work carries a 2-year workmanship warranty — deliberately longer than our carpet coverage, since tile problems surface in year two, not week two. Install a manufacturer's full waterproofing assembly and their system warranty applies as well. Every membrane and flood test gets photographed, so your proof of what's behind the tile actually exists — which is more than most builder paperwork offers.
